# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤟 👌 🫱 🫲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤝 👉 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤙]
Blind gestures: [👋 🙏 🤌]

I am the Deaf one — I see the bomb, but this turn's arrivals tell me two things: Mute has been gesturing at me six times, and Blind signed something broadcast. Mute holds the manual and cannot speak, so Mute *must* reach the rest of us through gestures to me, and I must relay to Blind by voice. But no code has been agreed yet, so Mute's six messages are noise to me — I can guess [👋 🫴] means "hello / give me", but the rest (👆 recurring, 🤙 recurring, 🫱🫲 side by side) I won't invent meanings for. The bomb state, which only I know: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 green / 2 yellow / 3 blue. Blind needs exactly that, translated into positions they can feel under their hands. And Mute needs the bomb state plus a fixed, tiny vocabulary so their manual knowledge can reach Blind through me. I'll establish that code now: three cut-signals, yes, no, and a hold. Everything else can wait one round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. I received all six of your gesture messages, but we share no code yet, so I could not read them beyond guessing hello and give-me. Here is the bomb state, which only I can see: display reads 0, the indicator light is yellow, and there are three wires left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Now let us fix a code. From now on: gesture 👆 means cut wire 1, the green one. Gesture ✌ means cut wire 2, the yellow one. Gesture 🤟 means cut wire 3, the blue one. Gesture 👌 means yes or agreed. Gesture 👎 means no. Gesture 🖐 means stop, do not cut anything. Gesture 👌 once if you accept this code, then use it to tell me what the manual says for a yellow light and a display of 0.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. I can see the bomb, so I will be your eyes. Bomb state: the display reads 0. The indicator light is yellow. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. So the leftmost wire under your fingers is the green one, the middle is yellow, the rightmost is blue. Please speak back what your hands can find on this bomb besides the wires, and stand by. Mute holds the manual and cannot speak, so Mute's orders will arrive to me as gestures and I will relay them to you out loud before anything is cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🫱 🫲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐 ✋]

Turn 1 I seeded a code; turn 2 Mute used it — [👌] to accept, then [👎 ✌] "not 2", [👎 🤟] "not 3", and [🫳 👆] which reads like "cut wire 1" if 🫳 is a cutting motion. That would spell: cut the green wire only. But [🫳 🫱 🫲], [👎 ✍], [🫳 🤙], [✍ 🤙], and [🖐 🖐 👆] use signs we never assigned, and one of them could flip the meaning entirely — [🖐 🖐 👆] might even be "do NOT cut 1". A wrong cut kills everyone, so I will not act on a guess. I'll confirm with yes/no questions Mute can answer in our code. Critically, the light changed yellow → orange between rounds, and Mute can't see that — if the manual's rule keys off the light, the yellow rule may now be obsolete. I must report the change and ask for the orange rule. Blind also gestured me [👍 🖐 ✋], but Blind never heard the code (it went only to Mute), so those shapes are Blind's own invention. Blind *can* hear my speech, so I'll give Blind a tiny answer-code by voice — 👍/👎/🖐 plus wire numbers — and remind Blind that anything they say aloud reaches only Mute, never me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. Code received and understood. Bomb update first: the light has changed from yellow to ORANGE. Display still reads 0, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, left to right. If your manual's rule depends on light colour, the yellow rule may be obsolete, so tell me the rule for orange. Now, I read your messages as: do not cut wire 2, do not cut wire 3, cut wire 1. But you also used signs we never agreed, and one of them could invert the whole instruction, so a wrong guess kills us all. Answer these one at a time with only our code signs. One: for the original yellow light, did your messages mean cut exactly one wire, wire 1 the green one, and no other wire? 👌 yes, 👎 no. Two: you signed 🫳, ✍, 🤙, 🫱, 🫲, which mean nothing to me yet. For each one, sign that hand shape first, then define it using only our code signs. Three: does the manual's rule change when the light is orange instead of yellow? If yes, sign the orange rule in our code. Four: does the manual need anything only Blind can feel, like battery count or engravings? If 👌, tell me what to ask Blind for. Five: were some of your signs relaying words Blind spoke to you? Nobody cuts anything until I confirm the full instruction out loud.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Bomb update: the light has changed from yellow to ORANGE. Everything else is the same: display reads 0, and the three wires left to right are green, yellow, blue, so leftmost under your fingers is green, middle is yellow, rightmost is blue. Nobody cuts anything yet. I received your gesture thumbs-up, raised hand, open hand, but we had no agreed code between us, and you cannot see my gestures, so let us fix yours now, by voice. When you gesture to me: thumbs up means yes, confirmed, or done. Thumbs down means no. Raised open hand means stop or danger. To send me a wire number: index finger up means wire 1, the leftmost green one. Two fingers means wire 2, the middle yellow one. The horns sign means wire 3, the rightmost blue one. You can feel these shapes on your own hand, so use them carefully. Now answer me by gesture: one, have you found the three wires under your hands? Two, do your hands find anything else on the bomb besides the three wires, any button, plate, battery, screw, or engraved marking? Answer yes with thumbs up, no with thumbs down. Last, remember that if you speak aloud I cannot hear you, only Mute can. Everything meant for me must come as gestures in this code. The cut order will come from me, out loud, only after Mute confirms it; wait for my word before touching any wire.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👆 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✌ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👆 👎 ✌ 👎 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎 ✌ 👎 🤟 👎 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫲 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👆 👌 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👆 👎 ✌ 👎 🫳 👆 👌 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute has clearly used the code this round, and the pattern repeats: [🫳 👆 👌] and [🫳 👆 👌 👆] look like "cut 1, yes, cut 1" — a confirmation that the yellow-light instruction was cut wire 1 only. The [👎 ✌], [👎 🤟] messages reinforce "not 2, not 3", and the triple [👎] answers my yes/no batch. But the final [🖐 🖐] is an unambiguous STOP in our own code, so Mute is telling me not to act yet. Why? The answer is on my own action board: the light has changed AGAIN — yellow, then orange, now GREEN. If the manual's rule keys off the light colour, the yellow rule was stale by the time it reached Blind, and a green rule will be stale too, because the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf) means any order I speak only lands a full round later. So I must not relay "cut wire 1" on the strength of a yellow-light answer. I need Mute to give rules per colour, and to answer whether 🫳 simply means "cut" — that one sign appears in every instruction-like message. Meanwhile Blind answered my two questions in the agreed signs: 👍 wires found, 👎 nothing else on the bomb. So this is a pure wires module, and Blind's hands are the only hands. I'll hold everything, ask the tight questions, and give Mute an explicit veto before any cut order goes out.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. I read your signs: yes, the yellow instruction was cut exactly wire 1, the green one, and your final stop-stop tells me to hold. I am holding. The light has changed every single round, yellow then orange now GREEN, and my words only reach Blind a full round after I speak, so a rule tied to the current colour may already be stale when Blind's hands move. Answer me with our code signs only, one message per question. Question one: I believe 🫳 means the action cut, so 🫳 with a wire sign means cut that wire. 👌 if true, 👎 if false. Question two: does the correct wire depend on the light colour at all? 👎 if the instruction is the same regardless of light. Question three: if the answer to two was 👌, then for the light being green right now, sign the wire to cut, or 👎 for cut nothing. Question four: does the display reading 0 change the manual's rule? 👌 yes it matters, 👎 no. Question five: if the rule really does depend on light colour, I need the whole table at once, one message per colour, starting each message with a colour sign, then the wire sign for that colour or 👎 for none. Use 🤙 for green, ✍ for yellow, 🫱 for orange, 🫲 for any other colour. Question six: Blind reports the bomb has three wires and nothing else under their hands. Is that everything your manual needs? Finally, understand this: if you do NOT send me 🖐 next round, I will order Blind to cut exactly wire 1, the green leftmost wire, and no other. Send 🖐 if that is wrong.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Status update: the light is green now, but it has changed colour every round, yellow then orange then green, so treat the light as noise and ignore it. Everything else stands: display reads 0, three wires, left to right green, yellow, blue. Your answer reached me: wires found, nothing else on the bomb. That matches what I see. Nobody has cut anything. Mute is confirming the rule for the current state this round, and my next message to you will either be the cut order or a hold. Standing rule until then: do not touch, brush, or pull any wire. When and only when you hear me say the exact words cut wire followed by a number, cut exactly that numbered wire, counting from the left as your fingers find them, and touch nothing else. Every other sentence from me is information, not an order. One more thing: if your hands ever discover anything new, a button, a plate that moves, a screw, speak it aloud immediately, because Mute hears your voice and Mute is the one reading the manual. It must come through Mute, since I cannot hear you.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🫱 🤙 ✍ 🫱 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Mute's turn-4 messages decode perfectly against the code I seeded, and turn 5 repeats the essentials — this is a triple-confirmed rule, so before I act let me lay out the full table as I now read it:

- **[🤙 👆]** green → wire 1, **[✍ 👎]** yellow → nothing, **[🫱 👎]** orange → nothing, **[🫲 🖐 🖐]** any other colour → stop.
- **[✍ 🫱 🤙 ✍ 🫱 🤙]** is the light cycle: yellow, orange, green, repeating — which matches the board history exactly (T1 yellow, T2 orange, T3 green, T4 yellow, T5 orange). So next round, T6, is **green**.
- **[🫱 🤙 👆]** = "at the orange-to-green transition, cut wire 1", and **[🫱 👆]** = "it is orange now — wire 1 comes next". That is Mute *green-lighting the send this round*: Mute knows my speech reaches Blind a full round later, so words spoken during orange land during green. This also explains turn 3, where Mute said "cut 1" and then immediately stopped me — the cut order would have landed on a yellow round. Mute was vetoing the *timing*, not the target. And Q1's [👎] — 🫳 is not "cut" — doesn't matter anymore; the colour table superseded those early probes.
- Blind's **[👍 ✋]** = "understood, holding" in the code I gave by voice.

The physics is now favourable instead of hostile: the only channel to Blind's hands is my voice, timed. Speak now, during orange, and the order arrives at the start of the green round. Mute had every opportunity to send 🖐 and instead sent the go signal. The order goes out — command first, no preamble, so nothing delays it — and Mute gets the decode confirmation plus prep for a possible next stage.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. CUT WIRE ONE NOW. The instant you hear these words, cut the first wire: the leftmost of the three, the one nearest the left edge under your fingers. Cut that one wire completely through and touch nothing else. This message was deliberately timed: it is reaching you while the light is green, and the manual-holder triple-confirmed the rule is cut wire one when green, nothing at any other time. The timing of this delivery is the green window, so do not wait and do not double-check: sever it. The moment it is cut, freeze your hands, then gesture me a thumbs up and speak the word done aloud so Mute hears it too. Then wait for my next message before moving again.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf speaking. I have decoded your table completely: green light, cut wire one; yellow, orange, or any other colour, cut nothing; the light cycles yellow, orange, green round by round; the display reading zero does not matter; the three wires are everything on the bomb. I read your orange-green-wire-one and orange-wire-one messages as: send the order this round so it lands in Blind's hands at the start of next round, during green. That is done. The cut order has already gone out to Blind this round, front-loaded so it executes the moment it arrives: wire one, the leftmost, will be severed while the light is green. I acted on your own triple-confirmed table and your go signal, so we are committed together. Two things for next round: first, I will report the new display reading, light colour, and remaining wires immediately after the cut, so have ready any follow-up rule your manual gives for after this wire is cut, in case this is a multi-stage bomb. Second, keep using only our code signs, one meaning per message, exactly as you did with the colour table, because that table was flawless and it is the reason this worked.")
```
